requirement: Judge whether an aware instant is within 09:00 to 17:00 weekday hours in an IANA zone, and compute the UTC opening instant for a local date so it shifts across daylight-saving changes, rejecting naive instants and unknown zones.
skeleton: OPEN and CLOSE time constants, business_zone wrapping ZoneInfo lookup errors, is_open converting to the zone before checking weekday and a half-open time range, and opening_utc combining the date with the zone and converting to UTC.
caption: Local business hours with the standard-library zoneinfo and datetime modules. OPEN is nine o'clock and CLOSE is seventeen o'clock. business_zone(name) returns ZoneInfo(name) and turns ZoneInfoNotFoundError or ValueError from the lookup into ValueError naming the unknown time zone, chained from the original. is_open(instant, zone) raises ValueError saying the instant must be timezone-aware when tzinfo is None, converts the instant to the zone with astimezone, and returns True only on Monday to Friday when the local time is at or after OPEN and strictly before CLOSE. opening_utc(day, zone) combines the calendar date with OPEN using the zone as tzinfo and converts the result to UTC, so the same local opening maps to different UTC hours before and after a daylight-saving switch. The fixture asserts that in America/New_York the opening is 14:00 UTC on Friday 6 March 2026 and 13:00 UTC on Monday 9 March, that 13:30 UTC is open on the Monday but not on the Friday, that 20:59 UTC Monday is open while 21:00 UTC is closed, that Saturday is closed, and that a naive datetime and the zone Mars/Olympus_Mons raise ValueError.

plan.intent: Tell whether a shop is open at a given moment
constraints: Hours are 09:00 inclusive to 17:00 exclusive, Monday to Friday, in the shop's zone

rationale.teaches: ZoneInfo with astimezone for local-time decisions and datetime.combine with a zone tzinfo for local-to-UTC conversion.
rationale.why: Time code that compares UTC clock times, assumes a fixed offset, or accepts naive datetimes is right for half the year, so the dates must straddle a daylight-saving switch to catch it.

ops.docstring: Decide whether an instant falls inside a shop's local business hours.

ops.stmt: from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, time

candidates.why_wrong: Seventeen o'clock itself counts as open.
The weekday check admits Saturday, so the shop looks open on weekends.
The instant is never converted, so UTC clock time is compared against local hours.
Naive datetimes are silently interpreted in the machine's local zone.
The opening is built in UTC instead of the shop's zone, so it is 09:00 UTC all year.
